query: What plugs and voltage do they use in the UK?
answer:
The UK uses the Type G plug, defined by British Standard BS 1363. It has three rectangular pins in a triangle, and every plug has a fuse inside [1][2]. Mains power is 230 V at 50 Hz [1][2].

If you're coming from the US or Canada (120 V, 60 Hz), a plug adapter only changes the shape of the plug. It doesn't change the voltage [2]. Look at the label on each device. Most phone and laptop chargers say "100–240 V," which means they'll work with just an adapter. Something rated only for 120 V, like many hair dryers, needs a voltage converter or it can be damaged. One search result said the voltage can vary by ±10%. From what I know, the UK's legal range is actually +10%/−6% (about 216–253 V), but I didn't find a source to confirm that.
